title: Add iso8601_to_nstime() for editcap and nettrace
description:
This adds a function to parse a string date-time in ISO 8601 format into a `nstime_t` structure. It's based on code from epan/tvbuff.c and wiretap/nettrace_3gpp_32_423.c and meant to eventually replace both. (Currently only replaces the latter, since that's code I've already recently touched in !1275.)

Since most of Wireshark expects ISO 8601 date-times to fit a fairly strict pattern, iso8601_to_nstime() currently rejects date-times without separators between the components, even though ISO 8601 actually permits this. This could be revisited later.

Also uses iso8601_to_nstime in editcap to parse the -A/-B options, thus allowing the user to specify a time zone if desired. (See #17110)

notes.body: Note that, despite the changes to the editcap documentation, it still accepts a space (not just a 'T') between the date and time components of the -A/-B options.

added 1 commit
  • 36f8ba27 - Fix pipeline failures
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/1618/diffs?diff_id=134508535&start_sha=346f99bf27a90e4fc8db3a06eb2068cbc8d964ad)

> Note that, despite the changes to the editcap documentation, it still accepts a space (not just a 'T') between the date and time components of the -A/-B options.

The documentation should probably say that both are accepted.
How does this sound? "For compatibility with earlier versions of editcap, a space may be used in place of the 'T' separator." It would appear on the man page at the end of the -A and -B options.

YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS is referred to as "ISO 8601" format enough, and is used enough (we offer it as a display format and *don't* offer the format with "T" as a display format, and that format is also supported in Wikipedia templates, for example) that I wouldn't say "you *should* use the T, but, for backward compatibility, we'll let you use a space, too".

I'd just say that either YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS are accepted, without giving the latter pride of place.

commits_data.title: Editcap docs: specify 'T' or ' ' allowed
commits_data.message:
Editcap docs: specify 'T' or ' ' allowed

Clarify that the date-time specification can use either a 'T' or a space
as a delimiter between date and time.
